paragraphs.source_en: Based on this, we can see that even with no other income, by age 90 our taxpayer’s RMD of $154,719 will put them in the 28% tax bracket even without considering any other income. And that’s based on starting with only $1,000,000. Many readers applying the principles in this book starting in their 20s, 30s and 40s can easily expect to have several multiples of that by the time they reach 70 1/2.

units.source_en: Based on this, we can see that even with no other income, by age 90 our taxpayer’s RMD of $154,719 will put them in the 28% tax bracket even without considering any other income.
And that’s based on starting with only $1,000,000.
Many readers applying the principles in this book starting in their 20s, 30s and 40s can easily expect to have several multiples of that by the time they reach 70 1/2.

paragraphs.source_en: Something that is important to note here—which confuses many people—is that this doesn’t mean they pay 28% of the full $154,719 in taxes. Rather they pay 28% only on the amount over the $151,900 threshold of the bracket. The rest is taxed at the lower brackets on down. Should their other income bump them over the $231,450 threshold for the 33% bracket by, say, one dollar, they will only pay 33% in tax on that one dollar.
